name: HaloModel sources
description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Halo's window: HaloProject (compositions, the selected one, unique names), HaloTimeline (each composition's playhead, timecodes, the layers active at a frame, the strip's rows, in and out points at the playhead), HaloLayer (kind, span, color, opacity, CoreRaster blend mode, solid rectangle, a solid's or shape's gradient Fill in a unit box, a shape layer's SuiteKernel ShapeSpec; HaloFill+Kernel makes the project SuiteKernel's GradientFillTarget and HaloShape+Kernel its ShapeTarget), FrameRenderer (composites a composition's solids into one preview frame with CoreRaster), HaloStatusText (the inspector header, Composition rows and status-bar timecode text), the New Composition draft and its validated settings, RefusedRename, which keeps a refused composition rename for the alert, and the inspector TEXT section's rules (HaloTextDraft, a field draft kept with its layer; the refusals TEXT owns; the size bar's drag range), and the adapter onto SuiteKernel's Keys (HaloEasing+Kernel: HaloKeyRef, HaloKeySegment, HaloEasingPreset and HaloKeyState map to KeyRef, Segment, EasePreset and KeyState; handles and key rules run on EaseCurve and KeyRules), and the adapter onto SuiteKernel's LayerTree (HaloLayers+Kernel: a composition's layers as a single-level tree whose follow link is each layer's parentID; moves, bring/send, duplicate, world placement and the parent picker run on it), and HaloHeadless (the CLI's headless document: opens, saves and makes a project, runs HaloProject's catalog with file commands left to the CLI, and renders one frame to PNG through HaloFramePNG, an 8-bit RGBA writer used while core's PNG writer refuses; movies stay on macOS), and HaloMenuState (what a menu item built from its catalog spec reads: the focused window's project, every item off without one, titles from title(for:), runs through the catalog), and the recovery adapter (HaloRecovery+Kernel: the project as SuiteKernel's HistoryJumping, its History panel listing from the kernel History, and the recovery copy's bytes in HaloFiles' encoding).
